chunks: Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

“Look at the children who are with you, then bring them forward to al-Juḥfah or to Baṭn Marr, and do for them what is done for the muḥrim. Ṭawāf is performed with them, pebbles are cast on their behalf, and whoever among them does not find the hady, his guardian should fast on his behalf. And ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام used to place the knife in the hand of the child, then the man would grasp his hand and slaughter.”

key_terms.وَلِيُّهُ: his guardian who acts on his behalf
key_terms.ٱلسِّكِّينَ: the knife used in the act of slaughter
key_terms.ٱلْمُحْرِمِ: a person in the state of ihram whose rites and restrictions apply
key_terms.ٱلْهَدْيَ: the sacrificial offering due in the hajj rite

ai.seo_question: How should children be assisted in performing the rites of hajj according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal guidance regarding children performing hajj rites under the supervision of their guardians. It explains that children are to be treated like those in ihram, with certain rites carried out on their behalf, and it also preserves the practice of Imam ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام regarding sacrificial slaughter for a child.
